text: Fresh tiger pugmarks on the sandy bank of the Kolhi stream, heading north. Large male by the size, about 14 centimetres across the pad. Camera trap CT-112 photographed the same tiger at 02:40.
A leopard took a goat from a shed at the edge of Pimpri village at night. The owner filed a claim; inspection note on Form HW-3 written the next morning. Pugmarks and drag marks confirmed a leopard.
Camera trap CT-117 missing from its tree on the path to the Sambar water hole. The strap was cut. Reported to Vanrai Base and Form CT-9 filed. Daily patrols started in B-07.
Two wire snares found 300 metres from where CT-117 was taken, set on a deer path. Photographed, removed and bagged as evidence. No animal caught.
A visitor vehicle stopped off the road near viewpoint 2 to photograph a herd of spotted deer. The guide was warned and the trip sheet notes the breach.

Smoke seen from tower T3 at a bearing of 220 degrees. Tower T1 reported the same smoke at 160 degrees. A ground fire of about two hectares in the grassland was put out by a crew of six in three hours.
Gaur herd of fourteen grazing in the fields near Kolhi Gate at dusk. One lone bull stayed close to the road. Villagers were asked to keep their cattle away for the evening.
Sloth bear with two cubs seen digging at a termite mound beside the patrol route. The patrol pair stopped, clapped, and the bear moved off. No contact.

A villager from Rajur was bitten on the ankle by a snake while cutting grass. The bite was kept still, and the man was carried to the Primary Health Centre at Rajur and given anti-venom. He recovered.
A drone was flown over the tourism zone from outside Ghatmatha Gate at 16:20. No P-7 permit had been issued. Direction and time noted and reported.
Elephant dung and broken bamboo along the river path. Fresh, probably two days old. The herd seems to be moving north earlier than usual.
Vultures gathering over a ravine. A dead sambar was found, killed by wild dogs, not poachers: bite marks only, no wire, no wounds from weapons.
Camera trap CT-117 was replaced with a new unit on a higher tree. Batteries and card set; next change due in 21 days.
A pair on night patrol missed two check-ins because the radio battery failed. Vanrai Base sent a vehicle; the pair was found safe at the beat camp.
Wild pigs damaged a groundnut field near Pimpri. Three farmers filed claims with photographs and a panchnama within 48 hours.
Tigress with two cubs photographed by CT-104 near the Bhavani water hole. First record of cubs in B-01 since 2023.
Fire line along the B-03 boundary found overgrown in two places. Cleared by the beat crew the same day.
A leopard rested on the rock at viewpoint 1 for twenty minutes during the evening safari. Nine vehicles stopped; all kept to the road.
Strangers on a motorcycle on the forest road after closing time, near the old quarry. Vehicle number noted and given to Vanrai Base. Not confronted.
Crown fire on the southern slope of B-05 during strong wind. The crew withdrew to the fire line on the river road and waited. The fire stopped at the line after burning about 40 hectares.
Leopard seen inside Rajur village near the school at dawn. People were kept back and Vanrai Base called. The rapid response team waited; the leopard left by itself within an hour.
Researchers from the wildlife institute walked the B-02 route with the beat guard to count hornbill nests. Seven active nests found.
Elephant herd of eleven crossed the river at the southern ford. Patrol kept 150 metres back and turned off the route until the herd had passed.
Batteries and memory cards changed on CT-113 to CT-120. CT-117 images show a leopard, two sambar and a porcupine; no people.
